claims.statement: Raloxifene is a benzothiophene-derivative selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM), marketed as Evista (raloxifene hydrochloride); its structured-database identifiers are PubChem CID 5035, DrugBank DB00481, CAS 84449-90-1, and UNII YX9162EO3I.

extractedEvidence.quote: CAS Number: 84449-90-1; UNII: YX9162EO3I; Molecular Formula: C28H27NO4S
Raloxifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that is used to prevent and treat osteoporosis and reduce the risk of invasive breast cancer in high-risk postmenopausal women.

reviewFlags: CAS/UNII sourced from a commercial chemical-supplier database (chemicalbook.com), not a government registry; corroborate against FDA GSRS/UNII resolver or ChemIDplus at review time

claims.statement: FDA-approved EVISTA (raloxifene hydrochloride) labeling covers two indications in postmenopausal women: treatment and prevention of osteoporosis, and reduction of risk of invasive breast cancer in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis or at high risk for invasive breast cancer.

context.useCase: osteoporosis treatment/prevention; breast cancer risk reduction
context.doseText: Label-indicated dosing context, not a use recommendation.

extractedEvidence.quote: Treatment and prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women
reduction of invasive breast cancer risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis or at high risk

claims.statement: EVISTA carries an FDA boxed warning for increased risk of venous thromboembolism (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, retinal vein thrombosis) and for increased risk of death due to stroke in a trial of postmenopausal women with documented coronary heart disease or elevated coronary risk; the drug is contraindicated in women with active or past history of venous thromboembolism and in pregnancy.

context.population: postmenopausal women, including subgroups with coronary heart disease or elevated coronary risk

extractedEvidence.quote: Increased risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism have been reported with EVISTA.
Increased risk of death due to stroke occurred in a trial in postmenopausal women with documented coronary heart disease or at increased risk for major coronary events.
EVISTA is contraindicated for use in pregnant women

claims.statement: Raloxifene acts as a selective estrogen receptor modulator, binding estrogen receptors to produce tissue-selective estrogen-agonist effects (e.g., decreased bone resorption and increased bone mineral density) alongside estrogen-antagonist effects in other tissues such as breast and endometrium.

extractedEvidence.quote: Binding to estrogen receptors. This binding results in activation of estrogenic pathways (estrogen-agonistic effect) and blockade of estrogenic pathways (estrogen-antagonistic effect).

claims.statement: In the MORE randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (7,705 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, 180 centers, 25 countries, median 40 months follow-up), raloxifene reduced the risk of invasive breast cancer versus placebo: 13 cases among 5,129 women on raloxifene vs 27 among 2,576 on placebo (relative risk 0.24, 95% CI 0.13-0.44, P<.001); estrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer risk was reduced by 90% (RR 0.10, 95% CI 0.04-0.24).

context.population: postmenopausal women with osteoporosis (mean age 66.5, 96% white, no prior breast cancer)
context.useCase: breast cancer risk reduction (approved indication, secondary trial endpoint)
context.doseText: 60 mg or 120 mg/day in the MORE trial protocol; trial dose context, not a use recommendation.

extractedEvidence.quote: Thirteen cases of breast cancer were confirmed among the 5129 women assigned to raloxifene vs 27 among the 2576 women assigned to placebo (relative risk [RR], 0.24; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.13-0.44; P<.001).

reviewFlags: trial population is postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, not a general breast-cancer-risk population; do not generalize beyond labeled population

claims.statement: In the MORE trial, raloxifene significantly increased the risk of venous thromboembolic disease relative to placebo (relative risk 3.1, 95% CI 1.5-6.2), independently corroborating the magnitude of the VTE risk described qualitatively in FDA boxed-warning labeling.

context.population: postmenopausal women with osteoporosis enrolled in the MORE trial

extractedEvidence.quote: Raloxifene increased the risk of venous thromboembolic disease (RR, 3.1; 95% CI, 1.5-6.2)

claims.statement: Anabolic-androgenic-steroid-using bodybuilding forums promote self-directed raloxifene dosing (posts described protocols ranging from 30-120 mg/day, including a 17-week taper starting at 120 mg/day) to reverse gynecomastia, citing a pediatric case series ("J Pediatr. 2004") reporting 91% of raloxifene-treated patients improved and "no side effects were seen in any patients"; no controlled human trial of raloxifene for gynecomastia in adult anabolic-steroid users was identified, the cited pediatric population and setting do not generalize to self-directed adult AAS-user dosing, and this use is not an FDA-approved indication.

context.population: adult male anabolic-androgenic-steroid users self-treating gynecomastia (forum-reported)
context.useCase: gynecomastia reversal during/after anabolic steroid use (popular online use, not an approved indication)
context.doseText: Forum-reported self-directed protocols (e.g., 60-120 mg/day tapering schedules); reported as-is from a user forum, not a trial protocol or a use recommendation.

91% receiving raloxifene [showed improvement]... 86% had significant decrease (>50%)... No side effects were seen in any patients

extractedEvidence.pageOrSection: Contraindications (illustrating label scope is limited to postmenopausal-women indications, not gynecomastia)

reviewFlags: misinformation-adjacent: forum dosing and 'no side effects' claims are drawn from a pediatric case series and self-report, not a controlled trial in adult AAS users
no approved indication or controlled human trial for gynecomastia in anabolic-steroid users was located; treat as evidence gap
do not cite forum dosing ranges as a use recommendation

conflicts.summary: FDA label and MORE-trial RCT data document a tripled risk of venous thromboembolic disease with raloxifene in postmenopausal women (RR 3.1), while the bodybuilding-forum source cites a pediatric case series claiming 'no side effects were seen in any patients' for a different population, dose pattern, and monitoring context; the anecdotal safety claim should not be read as contradicting the established VTE signal.

reviewReasons: Expansion-batch evidence packet requires human review before publication.
CAS/UNII identifiers were sourced from a commercial chemical-supplier database rather than a government registry (FDA GSRS/ChemIDplus); confirm at review time.
RxNorm and ChEMBL identifiers not yet resolved from structured databases.

Off-label bodybuilding/gynecomastia use in adult anabolic-steroid users is supported only by forum anecdote and an unverified secondary citation to a pediatric case series; no controlled human trial for this population/use was located and human evidence for this specific use is thin to absent.
